Mild nausea is common at the start. Eat: Mild nausea is common at the start. Eat slowly, stop when you feel full, and go easy on fatty food.
Your appetite may be smaller now. Put pr: Your appetite may be smaller now. Put protein first on your plate so you still reach your target.
Strength work two or three times a week: Strength work two or three times a week helps you keep muscle. Keep logging so your visits stay easy.
Oral GLP-1 tablets are absorbed best whe: Oral GLP-1 tablets are absorbed best when your stomach is empty. Take the tablet with only the amount of water your label says, then wait the time on your label before food, drinks or other medicines. Eating too soon can mean less of the medicine gets absorbed. If you are unsure about your wait time, ask your pharmacist.

When you eat less, protein helps protect: When you eat less, protein helps protect muscle. Many people aim for a portion of protein at every meal: Greek yogurt, eggs, cottage cheese, fish, chicken, tofu or a protein shake. Your care team can help you set a daily target that fits you.
Smaller meals, eating slowly and stoppin: Smaller meals, eating slowly and stopping at the first sign of fullness all help. Fatty, fried and very sweet food is often harder. Sip water through the day. If nausea is severe, you keep vomiting, or you have strong stomach pain, contact your clinician.
Less food often means less fiber and flu: Less food often means less fiber and fluid. Add vegetables, berries, oats, beans or a fiber supplement, and drink water through the day. Tell your clinician if it lasts more than a few days.
Follow the instructions on your medicati: Follow the instructions on your medication guide or ask your pharmacist. Do not take two tablets to make up for a missed one. Log a skipped day in the app so your visit summary stays accurate.
Open the Report tab a day before. Add th: Open the Report tab a day before. Add the questions you want to ask, then share the summary with yourself or your care team. Bring up any symptom that lasted more than a few days.
